# Ticket Review

`customer_support.support_management.ticket_review` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**What actually happened on this ticket, and what does it say about how we work?**


> Reading a specific ticket, or a specific set of them, to work out what happened and what it says about the system that produced it. Distinct from quality assurance in both sample and purpose: QA samples randomly to measure a population, review selects deliberately to understand an event — the reopen, the breach, the one the customer wrote in about twice. The subject is the path the ticket took rather than the agent who handled it, and the moment a review starts producing verdicts about people it stops producing findings about the process, because everyone present begins managing their exposure instead of reconstructing the timeline.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **experimental**


> Promote by adding outcomes, failure_modes, playbooks, heuristics, mental_models, decision_frameworks, kpis and handoffs, following quality-assurance in this subdomain. The expertise worth encoding: selection is the whole method — a review of tickets chosen because they went badly is a census of failure modes, and a review of tickets chosen because a manager noticed them is a census of what managers notice. The highest-yield selections are reopens, tickets with more than two owners, and anything the customer escalated after we thought it was closed. Also worth stating explicitly is that this capability shares almost all its inputs with postmortem and differs only in scope: one ticket rather than one incident.
